title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Enhancing EFL Writing Skills among High School Students
venue: Journal of Education and Human Sciences
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether artificial intelligence, specifically ChatGPT, can improve English as a Foreign Language (EFL) writing skills among high school students. The study focuses on core writing dimensions: task achievement, coherence and cohesion, lexical resource, grammatical range and accuracy, and overall writing skill. The central research question is whether using ChatGPT influences students’ writing performance.

The intervention consisted of an eight-week period in which students interacted with ChatGPT for AI-supported writing practice. ChatGPT was used to provide personalized feedback and suggestions on student writing, and the study also compared ChatGPT-generated evaluations with ratings from two expert English teachers, reporting over 90% agreement. Outcomes were measured using pre- and post-writing assessments scored with writing rubrics, and the authors analyzed score changes using paired-sample t-tests and repeated-measures ANOVA.

Participants were intermediate-level EFL students aged 14 to 16 at Al-Falah High School in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. The study was conducted in a secondary-school context and included 27 students, as indicated by the paired t-test degrees of freedom. There was no separate comparison group such as teacher-only feedback, peer-only feedback, AI-only versus other feedback conditions, or legacy automated writing evaluation; instead, the study used a one-group pre/post design.

The paper concludes that ChatGPT was associated with significant improvements in task achievement, coherence and cohesion, lexical resource, and overall writing skill. Reported mean scores increased notably in these areas, while grammatical range and accuracy showed a slight decline in mean score, which the authors identify as requiring further investigation. Overall, the paper argues that AI can be a useful supplement to EFL writing instruction, but should be integrated alongside traditional teaching rather than replacing teachers.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a single-group pre/post study without a direct comparator or control condition, so causal claims are limited despite reporting inferential statistics. It has some empirical rigor but does not meet quasi-experimental or randomized standards for stronger evidence tiers.
impact_tier_rationale: Reported within-subject effects on writing outcomes are substantial, with partial eta squared values ranging from .253 to .479 for multiple literacy subdomains and .299 overall, indicating medium-to-large impact in a priority secondary-school population. However, one writing dimension (grammar) declined, so the impact is strong but mixed across subskills.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT was used over an 8-week intervention with high-school EFL students to support writing practice through interactive responses, personalized suggestions, and dialogue-based assistance during writing tasks.
ChatGPT also functioned as an automated writing evaluation/feedback tool, providing feedback on student writing and generating grades that were compared with ratings from two expert English teachers.
The system was applied as an AI writing aid for EFL composition, aiming to improve task achievement, coherence/cohesion, lexical resource, and grammar in student essays.

finding.finding_summary: In a one-group pre/post study of high-school EFL students (n=27 inferred from df=26), overall writing skill improved significantly after 8 weeks of ChatGPT use, with total mean scores rising from 12.3 to 17.4; paired t-test results showed a mean difference of -2.296, t(26)=-3.331, p=.003, and repeated-measures ANOVA reported partial eta squared=.299. Subskills improved for task achievement (3.0 to 5.2; t(26)=-4.891, p<.001; partial eta squared=.479), coherence/cohesion (3.2 to 5.0; t(26)=-2.964, p=.006; partial eta squared=.253), and lexical resource (3.0 to 4.4; t(26)=-3.703, p=.001; partial eta squared=.345), but grammatical range/accuracy slightly worsened (3.0 to 2.9; t(26)=4.585, p<.001; partial eta squared=.447), making the literacy findings mixed overall.
finding.measure: Pre/post writing assessment rubric scores for overall writing skill, task achievement, coherence and cohesion, lexical resource, and grammatical range and accuracy
finding.effect_size: partial eta squared=.299 overall; .479 task achievement; .253 coherence/cohesion; .345 lexical resource; .447 grammar
finding.confidence_interval: Overall: 95% CI [-3.713, -0.879]; Task achievement: [-1.525, -0.623]; Coherence/cohesion: [-0.941, -0.170]; Lexical resource: [-0.979, -0.280]; Grammar: [0.531, 1.395]
finding.std_deviation: Overall paired-difference SD=3.582; Task achievement SD=1.141; Coherence/cohesion SD=0.974; Lexical resource SD=0.884; Grammar SD=1.091

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports that ChatGPT-generated grades showed over 90% agreement with evaluations from two expert English teachers, suggesting the tool may be useful for efficient automated assessment of student writing. However, no formal reliability coefficient, workload measure, or time-saved estimate was provided.
finding.measure: Agreement between ChatGPT-generated writing grades and ratings from two expert English teachers
